description: Kansas-only rules checked against the Kansas statutes and the Department of Revenue graduated-license page. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless a special hazard requires a lower speed, the maximum lawful speed Kansas sets in any urban district is
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-1558(a)(1) sets 30 mph in any urban district. The statute lists that figure as a maximum lawful speed.

questions.q: Kansas allows 75 mph on a separated multilane highway when
options: The highway is outside a city, even if no sign is posted
The secretary designates it and the limit is posted
The county commission asks for it
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-1558(a)(2) sets 75 mph on any separated multilane highway as designated and posted by the secretary of transportation. The 75 figure is not effective merely because the road is divided.

questions.q: The maximum speed K.S.A. 8-1558 sets on a county or township highway is
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-1558(a)(3) sets 55 mph on any county or township highway. That is lower than the 65 mph limit for other highways in (a)(4).

questions.q: A rural Kansas school zone, meaning the part of a highway outside a city that provides entrances and exits to an adjacent school, has
options: A statewide limit of 20 mph when children are present
A statewide limit of 15 mph during school hours
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-1560e does not publish one rural-school-zone speed. The secretary works with the district's board of education to determine the appropriate maximum and the appropriate signage.

questions.q: Kansas makes it unlawful to operate or attempt to operate a vehicle when the alcohol concentration in the person's blood or breath is
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-1567(a)(1) and (a)(2) use an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more in the person's blood or breath. Subsection (a)(2) also covers a 0.08 result measured within three hours of operating or attempting to operate.

questions.q: For a driver less than 21, Kansas makes it unlawful to operate or attempt to operate a vehicle with a breath or blood alcohol content of
options: Any alcohol at all, including a result under .02
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-1567a(a) says it is unlawful for any person less than 21 to operate or attempt to operate a vehicle with a breath or blood alcohol content of .02 or greater. That is a separate statute from the adult 0.08 offense.

questions.q: Driving a commercial motor vehicle under the influence includes an alcohol concentration in the person's blood or breath of
options: 0.08 or more only, the same as a passenger car
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-2,144(a)(1) and (a)(2) set 0.04 or more for operating or attempting to operate a commercial motor vehicle. A violation of the general DUI statute, K.S.A. 8-1567(a), is also included.

questions.q: Kansas treats a driver as a habitual violator when, within the immediately preceding five years, the driver has been convicted
options: Of offenses that add up to 12 demerit points
Three or more times of K.S.A. 8-285 offenses
Once of driving under the influence
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-285 defines a habitual violator by convictions, not by a demerit-point total. The definition requires three or more convictions, within the immediately preceding five years, of the offenses the section lists.

questions.q: When division records show that a person is a habitual violator, Kansas
options: Revokes driving privileges for three years, with the statutory exceptions
Adds a warning letter and leaves the privilege in force
Suspends the privilege only until the driver takes a course
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-286 says the division promptly shall revoke the person's driving privileges for three years, except as allowed under K.S.A. 8-235(d)(3) and 8-2110.

questions.q: One conviction that counts toward Kansas habitual-violator status is
options: Driving 6 mph over a 30 mph limit
A vehicle-equipment defect with no crash
questions.explanation: K.S.A. 8-285(a)(2) lists violating K.S.A. 8-1567, or a substantially conforming city ordinance, county resolution, or other state's law. Three such countable convictions in five years make the person a habitual violator.

questions.q: A Kansas instruction permit for ages 14, 15, and 16 requires a licensed adult in the front seat who is at least
questions.explanation: The Department of Revenue graduated-license page says an instruction permit at ages 14, 15, and 16 requires a licensed adult in the front seat at all times, minimum age 21. The permit must be held for 1 year to advance to a restricted license.

questions.q: At 15, a restricted Kansas licensee may not
options: Drive to school on a school day by the most direct route
Drive anytime when a licensed adult who is at least 21 is in the vehicle
questions.explanation: The Department of Revenue page bars any non-sibling minor passenger. Driving is limited to work, school on days when school is in session by the most direct route, a religious activity, or anytime with a licensed adult at least 21.

questions.q: From age 16 until 17, the lesser Kansas restrictions allow driving anywhere from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. and limit non-sibling passengers under 18 to
questions.explanation: The Department of Revenue page for less-restricted privileges at age 16 allows anywhere from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., with listed exceptions outside those hours, and no more than one non-sibling passenger under 18. A 50-hour affidavit is required.

questions.q: In Kansas, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Kansas issues a learner's permit for a car at 14 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Kansas, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Kansas requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 12 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Kansas complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Kansas requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Frequently Asked Questions About Teen Driving

questions.q: Of a Kansas teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Kansas requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

provenance.manual: Frequently Asked Questions About Teen Driving

questions.q: In Kansas, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Kansas, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 15 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Kansas not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Kansas restricts provisional drivers from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

provenance.manual: Graduated Driver License Requirements for Teen Drivers

questions.q: In Kansas, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Kansas drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Kansas car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Kansas car knowledge test has 25 questions.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Kansas car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Kansas car knowledge test.

questions.q: In Kansas, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Kansas sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: K.S.A. 8-1567a. Driving under the influence by any person less than 21 years of age

questions.q: In Kansas, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Kansas brings a suspension of 1 year.

provenance.manual: K.S.A. 8-1014. Suspension or restriction of driving privileges

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Kansas residential district?
questions.explanation: Kansas sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Kansas?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Kansas can be posted up to 75 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Kansas's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Kansas: only texting is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Kansas?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Kansas, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Kansas's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Kansas seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Seat Belts & Child Safety Seats | Kansas Highway Patrol

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Kansas?
questions.explanation: Kansas requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is Kansas's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Kansas requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
